_comment: kg-navigation, staged as a top-level named subgraph. Owner, 2026-09-20: '(kg-navigation should be similar named subgraph)' -- 'similar' to folio-assist-core, which had just been lifted out of cat-harness for the same reason. TOP-LEVEL and not `cat-harness/skills/kg-navigation/`, deliberately: `skills/` is ALREADY declared as this repository's `cat-harness` graph in full, so a nested entry would be a declaration inside a declaration, which is the defect #263's own comment names -- a consumer beneath the outer path cannot tell which declaration owns what it finds. A sibling directory has one owner and no ambiguity. WHY IT EARNS ITS OWN SUBGRAPH RATHER THAN A PACKAGE: the name was ALREADY carried by two different skill bodies in two instances -- `bootstrap/skills/kg-navigation.md` (72 lines, zero-install) and the tooled one moved here from `cat-harness/skills/folio-core/`. Two bodies under one name is not a duplicate to delete; they answer the same question under different preconditions. A named subgraph is what lets both be addressed without either shadowing the other.

directories.description: The TOOLED route -- what an agent takes when `skill_list`, `skill_fetch` and `work_plan_prime` are reachable. The zero-install floor stays in `bootstrap/skills/`, and MUST: bootstrap is phase one with nothing installed, and a bootstrap that reached into another instance for its first skill would fail in exactly the cold-start case it exists for. The id is NOT `cat-harness`; overrides match on the entry's id, and `cat-harness/harness.json` already holds that one for `skills/`, so reusing it would REPLACE the harness's knowledge graph rather than add to it.
